name: LS Pup
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 14.15 days; its mean radius is 79.3 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, LS Pup: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 79.3 +/- 2.1 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 116, Name='LS Pup', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5500 +/- 226 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, LS Pup: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 4470.1 +/- 120.8 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.461 +/- 0.015 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that swells and shrinks every 14.1 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 79.3 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 4,470 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, LS Pup: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)
